title: Release storyboard and microcopy screenshot suite for changelog blog
creator: Maya Chen
description: Produce a suite of release-focused visual assets and annotated screenshot storyboards for the upcoming Changelog blog post and release notes. Deliverables: high-resolution before/after UI composites, a 6-frame storyboard showing the onboarding quickstart flow, concise microcopy overlays for each frame, and web-optimized hero + thumbnail variants. Assets should be easily consumable by marketing, docs, and in-product changelog components.
acceptance_criteria: All hero and thumbnail images exported in JPG/WEBP/AVIF at required sizes
Six storyboard frames exported at 3x and annotated with microcopy callouts
Before/After composite demonstrating a specific UX improvement with an annotation layer
Accessible alt-text and a one-line caption for each image included in a CSV
Assets uploaded to Drive and linked in the ticket; final Figma file published and version-tagged
tasks: Define narrative beats for 6-frame storyboard in collaboration with PM
Draft microcopy for each frame and run micro-A/B with growth (text variants)
Create high-fidelity screenshots using staging environment (release-qa.redwood)
Compose before/after composite and callouts layer
Export assets in required sizes and formats, create low-bandwidth variants
Write alt text and one-line captions, assemble metadata CSV
Upload to Drive and link Figma file; tag release-2025.02 in Figma
Create GitHub PR documenting asset inventory and usage examples in docs repo
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff — aligned with PM on narrative beats and target audience (developers & tech PMs).
2025-02-14: Staging screenshots captured; discovered inconsistent theme tokens across components — raised ENG-2986.
2025-02-16: First draft microcopy reviewed by Steve Patel (PM) — feedback: shorten callouts to 3–6 words for thumbnails.
2025-02-18: Design review with Frontend — decided on subtle motion for hero micro-animations; confirmed feasible within web export constraints.
2025-02-20: Assets exported at 2x; accessibility pass in progress; preparing final upload to Drive.
review_feedback: Steve Patel (PM): Prefer active verbs in callouts; remove product-jargon in public-facing caption.
Lina Torres (Frontend Eng): Keep motion under 200ms loop and provide Lottie+static fallback.
Samira Reed (Content): Ensure every frame has a clear CTA or next-step microcopy for onboarding flows.
design_notes: Trade-offs: Micro-animations in hero add perceived polish but increase bundle weight. We will deliver a 200ms Lottie JSON and a static GIF fallback; marketing will choose per channel. For in-product changelog slots, use static WEBP to ensure fast load. Composition favors clarity over decorative elements — use a single accent color for callouts tied to Lighthouse brand tokens.
accessibility_notes: Provide concise alt-text entries for each asset and ensure color contrast for callouts meets AA. Include a text-only flow snippet in the release notes for screen-reader users. All exported fonts converted to outlines in flattened PNGs for consistent rendering.
notes: Follow up: schedule final review with Growth for social thumbnails (2025-02-24). Coordinate with ENG-2986 for component token fixes; do not block release if tokens cannot be fully reconciled — provide versioned fallback screenshots.
